_comment: The values the active theme cannot reach. Everything a React component renders reads semantic tokens and follows the theme by itself; these do not, because they are consumed outside React: an HTML <meta> the browser paints its chrome with, a webfont URL, a generated manifest, and a social card rendered by a node script. One theme swap edits this file and the import in __root.tsx. Values must match the corresponding tokens in src/theme/wtuTheme.ts.

manifest.name: WhichToUse — find the best AI tool for the job
manifest.description: SaaS, open source and agent skills across 25 areas of work, with the limits of each written down.

_iconNote: Icon tiles are white. The mark is a neon lockup drawn for a dark field and is composited onto white anyway, for the reason a favicon always is: browser chrome is a background we do not control, and a transparent mark inverts unpredictably between light and dark tab bars. White is also what the topbar already stands the same kind of artwork on, so the two agree. Its blue sits at 5.5 on white and its coral at 2.7 — the second is low for text, but this is a logotype and the pair is balanced, which is what makes the three letters read as one object.
_fontNote: One family, every job: Bricolage Grotesque across body, headings, labels and numbers. Inter is gone — it used to carry the interface while Bricolage was reserved for the wordmark, and this URL requested both. The request is the variable font's full 200-800 weight range plus the optical-size axis, because the interface now needs everything from 11px row text to display headings out of one file; narrowing it back to a few static weights will silently flatten the type scale. The URL must agree with typography.body/heading in wtuTheme.ts, and it is also what the social card in scripts/gen-icons.mjs renders with.
_markNote: The mark's colours, not the interface's. They are measured out of resources/wtu-logo-2.png, which every icon is rendered from; the two move together or neither does. Deliberately independent of the theme: the logo should not change colour because the product did. Only the social card reads them, to set 'WhichToUse' beside the mark in the mark's own colours, so w and u are the same value on purpose — the neon lockup paints 'w' and 'u' one blue and 't' coral. The retired monogram had three, one per letter, which is why this object is keyed by letter. Note that the topbar wordmark is a third asset again, on its own palette, and does not read these: 'Which' is the interface primary #4F46E5 and 'Use' is the prototype's deep teal #0E6E66, both applied by scripts/crop-wordmark.mjs, so the primary and the wordmark move together.
